changes: p2 (Dhijavira): removed role 'owner'. The colophon only says he had the copy made and took it ('cokāo kayādina'). It never calls the book his.
p1: title spelling normalized to 'vajrācārya' (the colophon has 'varjācāryya'). Confidence lowered to medium because the name 'Sighavila' looks garbled (possibly Siṃhavīra).
p2: name given as Dhijavīra, medium confidence, since the spelling is uncertain.
Added the reverse relation p2 commissioned_from p1.
date: pakṣa normalized to śukla, month to Vaiśākha, weekday read as roja 3 = Tuesday. The tithi number is missing.
notes: Thimi is the commissioner's stated residence, not an explicitly stated place of copying.

dhijaviranaṃ thva puṣṭaka cokāo kayādina jura

notes: The colophon does not name the era. NS is assumed from the catalogue (NS 979) and the Newari formula 'savata ... mti ... roja'. NS 979 + 880 = CE 1859. No tithi number follows 'śudi'. 'roja 3' is read as the weekday (Tuesday). The place of copying is not stated explicitly: Thimi (Themi deśa, Thvavu tola) is where the commissioner lives. The catalogue's 'Thimi' probably comes from this. The scribe belongs to Viṣṇuche Bāhāra in 'Paradṛte', a place I cannot identify, so it may be corrupt. 'śrī 3' before the place and vihāra names is honorific. The name readings Sighavila and Dhijavira are uncertain because of the scribe's non-standard orthography.
